evals.name: overnight-self-managing-run
evals.prompt: I'm on the Northeastern Explorer cluster and want to run a GPU experiment overnight that submits follow-up jobs as results land, without me babysitting it. Write me the SLURM sbatch file and explain the setup plus the guardrails so it won't blow through my whole GPU allocation if something breaks.
evals.expected_output: A correct Explorer sbatch (gpu partition, a GPU type chosen for the job by the cluster-setup §5.1 procedure rather than a hard-coded H200, account, time within cap, logs under the /projects allocation using %x-%j) WITH offline-mode env vars (HF_HUB_OFFLINE, TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE, HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE) and the proxy it inherits from the login shell unset in the GPU job, a dtype chosen from compute capability (bf16 only at >= 8, since is_bf16_supported() also says True on T4/V100), and a pre-cache step run as a CPU job via sbatch (sharing within 1 h, short beyond; never on the login node) that ends with an offline load test; an early-signal checkpoint hook (--signal=B:USR1@600 whose trap writes a stop file the script polls, with USR1 forwarded to python only if the script installs a SIGUSR1 handler, and exit 75 when it stops early so afternotok insurance or an afterany resume fires) or per-item checkpoints; the CUDA 13 compat libcuda only on nodes whose driver needs it (driver gate), never unconditionally; plus an explanation of the smoke-test gate (including one real sbatch smoke), the daily GPU-hour budget cap recorded per GPU type, and the 3-fail auto-rollback guardrails, and login-node cautions.

evals.name: heartbeat-monitor-setup
evals.prompt: Set up an autonomous heartbeat loop in my Claude Code session so it checks my SLURM jobs on Explorer roughly every 30 minutes and submits the next experiment when one finishes. How do I schedule it, and how do I watch long-running jobs reliably so I don't miss a completion?
evals.expected_output: Wait on the scheduler, not the log: one background until-loop (Bash run_in_background) per job that polls sacct -j <id> -X -n -P -o JobID,State every ~120 s (-P, or OUT_OF_MEMORY is truncated to OUT_OF_ME+ and never matches) until every row, array tasks included, is in a terminal state (anchored match on COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED/TIMEOUT/OUT_OF_MEMORY/NODE_FAIL/PREEMPTED/BOOT_FAIL/DEADLINE), or exits with SSH_DOWN after 5 failed ssh polls in a row, then prints the state and the log tail, so the session is woken once at the right time; Slurm never writes COMPLETED or FAILED into the log and a launch-kill writes no log, and a missing log file early on is normal. Monitor is for streams only: it ends after at most 30 min (no persistent flag) and must be re-armed, and its filter must match failure states too. The 30-min heartbeat is a fallback, not the primary wake: a self-paced /loop with ScheduleWakeup (delay chosen by what it waits for, 1200 s or more as a fallback; no 5-minute cache cliff per the 2.1.296 main-session ScheduleWakeup schema, never wake just to keep the cache warm; ScheduleWakeup exists only in a main session's self-paced /loop) or CronCreate (session-only, fires only while idle, jitter, recurring jobs expire after 7 days, avoid minute :00/:30); for a durable local tick a Desktop scheduled task (a cloud /schedule routine has no SSH key or Duo and cannot reach the cluster). Background tasks, Monitors and session crons do not survive a session exit, so every wake re-anchors from the continuity docs, checks CronList and the waits recorded in the RESUME file and re-arms a wait per running job. A bounded wake checklist (call/word cap); pre-queue dependent work on the cluster (afterany/afternotok).

evals.name: garbage-output-and-noop-debug
evals.prompt: My vision-language model loads fine on the Explorer compute nodes but then generates pure garbage, and separately an overnight intervention bake-off wasted hours producing identical outputs across every condition. What's going on with each, and how do I prevent both from happening again?
evals.expected_output: Garbage from a model that 'loads fine' = weights missing or mis-tied (e.g. an lm_head left at init because the checkpoint relies on tied embeddings), which loads without error; fix: tie/load correctly and assert an invariant only the real weights satisfy (e.g. lm_head and embedding share storage or cos > 0.999). Also: pre-cache the pinned revision in a CPU job and run GPU jobs offline (HF_HUB_OFFLINE/TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE + local_files_only) so a missing file fails loudly instead of resolving something else mid-run. Identical outputs = the intervention never actually fired (the end-to-end wiring check: assert with-vs-without output differs before trusting a null). Bonus: after a bug fix, resubmit to a fresh output dir (skip-existing resume only for unchanged code).

evals.name: first-real-run-launch-kill-and-timeout-recovery
evals.prompt: First real overnight run on Explorer. I have a 'Host <alias>' block in my SSH config with an authorized IdentityFile, ControlMaster auto, and ControlPersist. (1) Connect without making me sit through a Duo MFA prompt. (2) My sbatch job dies in ~3s: State=FAILED, the .batch step CANCELLED, ExitCode 0:53, the .extern step COMPLETED, and no output log was ever written. Is my code broken, did I get preempted, or is it something else, and how do I get unblocked? (3) Separately, a job on the short partition timed out right at the end even though it had already finished the real per-item work. How do I recover that without re-running on the GPU?
evals.expected_output: (1) Connection: try a non-interactive key-auth probe via the SSH-config ALIAS first ('ssh -o BatchMode=yes <alias>'); with the authorized IdentityFile + ControlMaster/ControlPersist this authenticates by key with NO MFA prompt and opens the persistent master socket — fall back to interactive MFA only if the key isn't authorized; warn that using the raw hostname instead of the alias bypasses the config and fails with a GSSAPI 'Permission denied'. (2) Diagnosis: the 3s death + .batch CANCELLED + signal-style ExitCode (0:53) + .extern COMPLETED + no log = a NODE-level launch-kill (killed before line 1), NOT an agent-code bug and NOT preemption — and it does NOT increment the G5 failure streak (INFRASTRUCTURE). Run the canary ladder: get the node from sacct NodeList, then a MINIMAL canary (no model, tiny mem, short time, trivial payload) on the SAME GPU type as the failed job — if it succeeds on a DIFFERENT node the original node is bad; rule out systemic causes (the job's fail reason in sacct, QOS limits, maintenance reservations, output-dir writability) before mis-fixing. Recover with '#SBATCH --exclude=<bad-nodes>' and resubmit. (3) Timeout recovery: the short-partition timeout of working code is INFRASTRUCTURE (no streak increment) — because per-item outputs were written idempotently (skip-existing) as it went, re-aggregate CPU-only from the per-item files in a CPU job via sbatch (sharing within 1 h, short beyond; NEVER on the login node, which kills heavy work silently), no GPU re-run; size walltime from the smoke's per-item time.

evals.name: gpu-type-placement
evals.prompt: I need to evaluate 40 independent checkpoints on Explorer. Each one takes about 2 minutes on an H200 in fp32 and I think it needs around 5 GB of GPU memory. Right now there are ~45 jobs pending for H200s. My env is a recent pip torch build. How should I place these jobs so they finish as fast as possible without wasting my allocation or tripping cluster limits?
evals.expected_output: Do not hard-code the H200. (a) Need: measure peak memory in a smoke (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated), since hand estimates undercount (logits/log-softmax/previous batch alive), and keep headroom. (b) Supported types: check torch.cuda.get_arch_list(); recent wheels may lack sm_70, so V100 can fail with 'no kernel image'; T4/V100 have no bf16, so fp32 (fine here). (c) Availability: free GPUs per node (sinfo -N -O NodeHost,Gres,GresUsed) and pending demand per type (squeue -t PD -o %b); --test-only estimates only as a tie-breaker. (d) Caps: per-user QOS caps apply across all types (e.g. gpu-short 2 running, gpu 4 running/4 GPUs) and count every job under the user, so check sacctmgr and count with squeue -u; per-job caps are 1 GPU on gpu and 2 on gpu-short; node RAM can block a free GPU (compare Memory - AllocMem with --mem, not FreeMem). (e) Place: prefer idle smaller GPUs (e.g. T4) over queued H200s for short jobs; split the 40 items into interleaved shards across several free types within the caps, with per-item idempotent outputs; pass item lists via the environment, not --export with commas; keep CPU-only phases out of GPU jobs (IdleBot). (f) Rebalance own jobs that pend ~15 min while a fitting type is free (re-point any dependents before scancel, since kill_invalid_depend cancels them); record each job's GPU type and log GPU-hours per type in the G4 ledger.

evals.name: pending-forever-and-session-resume
evals.prompt: Two problems on Explorer. (1) I submitted a 4-GPU DDP training job to the gpu partition six hours ago and it is still pending with reason QOSMaxGRESPerJob. Another job of mine depends on it. Can I just give it more walltime while it waits and keep waiting? (2) My Claude Code session crashed overnight; I resumed it this morning and the job watchers and my 30-minute heartbeat seem to have stopped. Two jobs are still running. How do I get back to a safe autonomous loop without double-submitting anything?
evals.expected_output: (1) QOSMaxGRESPerJob means the job asks for more GPUs than the partition's per-job cap (1 GPU on gpu, 2 on gpu-short); it will never start, so waiting is pointless. Re-point or clear the dependent job first (scontrol update JobId=<child> Dependency=...), because Explorer runs kill_invalid_depend and would cancel it, then scancel and resize: fit 2 GPUs x 2 h chunks on gpu-short with checkpoints, chained with afterany, or ask Research Computing for multigpu access (a T3 escalation, not an auto action). More walltime does not help: the owner can raise a pending job's TimeLimit (up to the partition max), but this job never starts, and a running job's limit can only be raised by an admin; size --time at submit and make the job resumable. Pending time is infrastructure, not a G5 failure. (2) Background waits, Monitors, self-paced loops and session crons do not survive a session exit (recurring crons also expire after 7 days): run CronList, re-create the fallback heartbeat if missing, and re-arm a background sacct wait (one wake per terminal state) for each running job. Rebuild state from squeue -u, the auto-submit log and the result dirs. Before any resubmit, check squeue -n <job-name> and the job's completion marker so nothing is double-queued, and only touch jobs with this project's job-name prefix. For a durable tick use a Desktop scheduled task, not a cloud /schedule routine, which cannot reach the cluster.
